newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks extend losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks extend losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks skidded lower at the close of an erratic session Wednesday, with Wall Street's slump offsetting the news of a possible sovereign debt upgrade, dealers said.

"The market slipped through technical support at 720 and may not bottom out before 680-690," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers. "The tone remains very volatile, mirroring the uncertain outlook of the U.S. markets."
The weighted MerVal index fell 1.2 percent to 717.97, wiping out early gains which took it to 729. It lost 2.1 percent Tuesday after a two-day bounce of 3.0 percent.

Traders said Banco Frances and Bansud banks bucked the trend and closed up 1.7 percent and 2.1 percent, respectively, on Standard & Poor's announcement Wednesday that it was placing Argentine debt under review for a possible upgrade.
Banco de Galicia, the only other MerVal-listed bank, surrendered gains at the close despite the good news which was expected to boost its bond holdings.
"Bonds were soft today because the U.S. long bond yield resumed its climb, undermining the stock market," another trader said.
Floor volume picked up to 32.6 million pesos from 29.1 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals firmed slightly to 143.8 million pesos.
The broad market eased 0.3 percent, with losers outgunning winners 35 to 18 and 14 issues closing flat.

Main-tier losses were led by textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, oil company Astra and carmaker Ciadea, which plummeted 5.0 percent, 4.7 percent and 3.9 percent, respectively. The best MerVal performer was foods giant Molinos, up 2.5 percent.
